title: Serving Rack Must Be Placed on Heat Mat; Stone Should Be Cleaned With Metal Scraper
text:
Serving Rack Must Be Placed on Heat Mat; Stone Should Be Cleaned With Metal Scraper. This JAMIE OLIVER PIZZA STONE AND SERVING RACK (round earthenware stone,14 inch) consists of a thin, lightweight stone that fits into a simple chrome-plated wire rack.

The rack is rather useless, because it only raises the stone about 3/8” from the surface it rests on, and requires hotpads or a heat mat underneath to protect that surface. (It's also questionable whether you’d want to serve a pizza at table on the stone taken directly from the oven, because the stone gets really HOT!)

The weight of the stone--very light for earthenware--is a plus. The 14” size is perfect for baking an 11” frozen pizza and getting a crispy crust. (My pizza was a frozen Newman’s Own Four-Cheese Pizza.)

However, the stone’s cleaning instructions add up to a huge minus. To wit: “It is best to scrape food residue off your stone with a metal spatula after the stone has cooled. It is recommended not to use water to clean your stone as this may leave moisture in the pores of the stone that may cause the stone to crack when heated in the oven.” The directions go on to say that if you must use water, you should use ONLY plain water (no detergent), and allow the stone to dry thoroughly before using it again.

The instructions also note that the “pizza stone will acquire stains through use”. That's absolutely true. After one use, my stone has burned-on residue and oil stains that make it unattractive for serving anything at all. (The stone is still perfectly functional for high-temperature baking, of course.) This product was a disappointment, because I wanted it for serving (with the rack).

As one of the world's best-loved chefs he continues to enjoy huge success on television and in publishing, with 12 television shows airing in over 100 countries and in excess of 23 million books sold to date. DKB household has worked closely with Jamie since 2005 when the hugely successful Flavor shaker was launched. Since then in excess of two million Flavor shakers have been sold in more than fifteen countries around the world. In 2009 the partnership was strengthened further by the launch of Jamie Oliver's kitchen kit, a range of easy to use and stylish kitchen products designed by Jamie and the DKB in-house design team. Following its success to date the kitchen kit range has been extended further to include more products which Jamie would be happy to use in his own kitchen. Jamie says "I'm really pleased with all the kitchen kit products the guys at DKB and I have developed over the years. I hope you'll like the new tools and gadgets we're introducing this year as much as I do".
